title: Proud Tek Leadership and Engineering Team
summary: Proud Tek is founder-led and engineering-first — a long-tenured team that has run RFID and NFC programs from chip-level integration through field deployment since 2008. This page covers who leads each functional area, the operating principles that shape how the team works, and how engineering escalation actually runs for a buyer program. Procurement teams that audit suppliers want to know who picks up the phone and who owns the outcome — this is that page. The independent editorial review board that signs off our published guides has its own page.
heroPoints: Founder and engineering lead with continuous RFID program experience since 2008.
Dedicated account engineer assigned per active program — same point of contact across reorders.
Independent technical review board signs off on the published RFID guides and comparison content.
imageAlt: Proud Tek organisation model — founder Peter Zhang over production engineering, independent quality, account engineering and supply chain, with one account engineer owning each program from RFQ to reorder

sections.title: Functional leadership
sections.intro: Proud Tek operates as a flat engineering-first organization. Each functional lead is responsible end-to-end for the line they own — from inquiry through dispatch — so buyer programs are not handed across silos that lose context between steps.

features.title: Founder and engineering lead
features.text: Peter Zhang. Founded Proud Tek in 2008 after a decade in contactless chip and inlay supply. Direct involvement in technical escalations, large-program scoping and editorial review of every guide on this site.

features.title: Production engineering
features.text: Owns the production floor for your program end-to-end — the same engineer from pilot through year-three reorder, so process context is never lost between steps. Line-by-line capabilities live on the Factory page.

features.title: Quality assurance
features.text: ISO 9001:2015 quality system, AQL sampling, calibration management, corrective-action follow-through. Independent of production scheduling — QA cannot be overridden by ship-date pressure.

features.title: Account engineering and sales
features.text: B2B account engineers (not 'sales people') handle the full inquiry-to-reorder lifecycle. Bilingual English / Chinese standard; Spanish and Arabic available on assignment.

features.title: Supply chain and procurement
features.text: Owns chip allocation, raw-material sourcing, freight and distributor safety-stock — so availability and lead time sit with someone accountable, not a broker in the middle.

features.title: Editorial and review board
features.text: An independent board — separate from sales — signs off the technical content on this site. It has its own page with named reviewers and a public corrections log.

sections.title: How engineering escalation actually works
sections.intro: Most buyer trust is won or lost during the first real engineering escalation — a reader-side error log, an anti-collision failure, a chip-specific encoding mismatch. The path below is how a typical issue moves from buyer's QA team to a corrected shipment.

items.label: Step 1 — Buyer signals the issue
items.text: Account engineer receives the issue (email, WhatsApp, support ticket) with the error context: reader make/model, firmware version, encoding sample, environmental conditions. We respond within one business day with an initial assessment.

items.label: Step 2 — Engineering replay in-house
items.text: Production engineering pulls the original encoding lot, replays the encoding scheme on a representative reader, and reproduces the issue if reader-side. Our test fleet covers the major reader brands (Impinj, Zebra, Honeywell, Feig, ACR, Chainway, Bluebird).

items.label: Step 3 — Root cause and corrective action
items.text: Findings reported back to the buyer with the root cause, the corrective action (chip substitution, encoding scheme adjustment, lamination tuning, etc.) and the impact on remaining inventory. Buyer signs off on the proposed correction.

items.label: Step 4 — Remediation and prevention
items.text: Corrected batch produced or screened-out lot replaced under our quality SLA. Corrective action filed in the ISO 9001 corrective-action register; future production travelers updated to prevent recurrence.

sections.title: How we operate — the principles behind the team
sections.intro: Proud Tek is deliberately a flat, engineering-first organisation. A handful of operating principles explain most of how the team behaves on a buyer program — and why the same call gets made whether or not anyone is watching.

features.title: Engineering-first, flat org
features.text: Decisions sit with the engineer closest to the chip and the line, not a management layer removed from the work — fewer hand-offs, faster technical answers.

features.title: One owner per program
features.text: The engineer who scopes your deal runs it for its life — RFQ, samples, pilot, production and reorder — instead of handing off to junior sales who don't know the chip-side trade-offs.

features.title: Quality independent of the ship date
features.text: QA reports separately from production scheduling and cannot be overridden by ship-date pressure. A lot that fails the 100% read test does not leave the building.

features.title: Factory-direct accountability
features.text: Owner-operated since 2008 — you deal with the factory, not a trading layer. When something goes wrong there is a named owner, not a supplier to point at.

features.title: Editorial integrity, audited
features.text: Published guides are reviewed by an independent board and corrections are logged publicly, because procurement teams check. See the review board and corrections log.

features.title: Predictable response
features.text: First response within one business day on qualified B2B inquiries; urgent escalations same business day in Shenzhen hours. Predictable timing over promised speed.

sections.title: How buyer programs get staffed
sections.intro: Program staffing follows a simple rule: the person who scopes the deal is the person who runs it for the life of the program. This is not aspirational — it is how the organization is structured.

before: Sales engineer scopes the deal, then hands off to a junior account manager who does not understand the chip-side trade-offs.
Account contact rotates every 12-18 months as headcount churns at the supplier.
Engineering escalation requires re-explaining the program context every time.
Reorders fall back to 'standard pricing' that ignores the negotiated terms of the original deal.
Quality issues bounce between sales and QA without a clear owner.
after: Same account engineer from initial RFQ through year-three reorder — they own the program.
Account engineers are owner-operator team members, not contract sales staff.
Engineering escalation routes straight to production — no re-explanation of context needed.
Reorders inherit the original commercial terms and engineering scope by default.
Quality issues have a documented owner (account engineer + QA lead) with SLA for response.

sections.title: Buyer support hours and response SLA
sections.intro: Predictable response timing matters more than promised speed. The SLA below is what we actually meet on qualified B2B inquiries, not a marketing target.
bullets: First inquiry response — within 1 business day (China Standard Time, Mon-Fri).
Urgent escalations — same business day during Shenzhen working hours (09:00-19:00 CST).
After-hours coverage — email and WhatsApp monitored outside business hours; non-urgent items queued for next-day reply.
Time-zone overlap — Asia-Pacific buyers get same-day; Europe buyers get same-day for issues raised before 14:00 CST; Americas buyers get next-day morning reply.
Holiday schedule — published in advance for Chinese New Year, National Day and other major holidays; safety-stock and pre-orders accommodate holiday lead-time gaps.

callout.label: After-hours and named-engineer coverage
callout.text: If your organization needs 24/7 support coverage for a critical-path program (e.g., live event RFID, hotel-lock retrofit during peak season), say so on the initial inquiry. We can structure a named-engineer arrangement with after-hours availability as part of an annual-volume agreement.

faq.question: Who actually picks up the phone if I email Proud Tek?
faq.answer: Account engineers respond to inbound inquiries within one business day. For new inquiries, the engineer assigned to your geography and product family takes the conversation. For existing programs, the engineer who scoped the original deal continues to own the relationship — including reorders, escalations and engineering follow-up.

faq.question: Is the engineering team in China or distributed?
faq.answer: All engineering, production and account engineering staff are located at the Shenzhen operation. We do not have overseas offices. Language coverage is English / Chinese standard, with Spanish and Arabic available by assignment. Time-zone overlap with European and American customers is managed through scheduled response windows.

faq.question: How long have your key engineering staff been with Proud Tek?
faq.answer: Founder and engineering lead has been continuously operating Proud Tek since 2008. Production engineering and account engineering staff have multi-year tenure — most senior engineers have been on the program for at least 5-10 years. We do not subcontract account management to short-tenure contract sales staff.

faq.question: What is the corrections process for technical content on the site?
faq.answer: Any reader can report a factual error in a published guide via the corrections-policy contact channel (see /about/corrections/). Reported issues are reviewed by the technical review board within five business days; substantive corrections are logged publicly with date, change and reason. We do not silently edit content to hide outdated claims.

faq.question: Do you disclose affiliate or supplier relationships in your guides?
faq.answer: Yes. The disclosures page (/about/disclosures/) lists current supplier, partnership and affiliate relationships that could influence the recommendation in a guide. Per-page disclosures appear at the end of any article where the relationship is relevant. We treat editorial integrity as a procurement-team trust signal, not a legal afterthought.
